issue.title: test_cache_miss_shows_loading_then_worker_result fails under the full parallel lane: WorkerFailed on an Event.wait timeout
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-p8.4 (epic sase-p8, 'sase pipe'), routed here by that epic's land agent. Unrelated to that epic's diff, which added a CLI hand-off command and touched no ACE/Textual code.

REPRODUCTION: failed once under sase-p8.4's escalated full parallel run (~32,685 tests) on 2026-08-18 with a WorkerFailed raised from an Event.wait timeout, and passed when rerun in isolation. Two other nodes failed in the same run and are tracked separately: test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet (sase-oz, +1 recorded there) and test_enter_loads_raw_definition_and_binds_source (filed alongside this bead).

WHY ITS OWN BEAD: sase-ct ('Flaky ACE TUI tests under full parallel just test run') is a RETIRED umbrella whose close reason forbids +1, and its retirement policy directs each observation to a node-specific bead named for the failing node. This is that bead for this node.

WHAT A WORKER NEEDS: the failure shape is a Textual worker that never signals its Event within the test's wait bound under CPU contention, so the load-dependent hypothesis to test first is scheduling starvation rather than a logic error — the same shape as sase-oz's 'a worker is still unfinished after the page exits'. Useful instruments: 'just test-contention -- <module>' (the tool sase-ct's retirement policy names) and running the module co-scheduled with the heaviest ACE modules rather than alone. Negative evidence is as valuable as positive here: record which lanes do NOT reproduce it, as sase-oz did.

RELATED: sase-j7 — in-progress epic 'Fix the sase-ct flake class at its root - process-global state leaking between tests' is the structural fix for this class; this node may be subsumed by it.
